status: Fixed in source; frozen runner publication and formal closeout remain separate states
finding: buildRootDropRelease inventories packages/**/dist but assumed its caller had already rebuilt those generated inputs. The runner reproducibility verifier built root-drop before onefile, while onefile then rebuilt package dist; the next root-drop pass therefore emitted a different release-manifest.json from the same source tree.
expectedBehavior: A root-drop release build must materialize its generated package-dist inputs before it derives the artifact inventory, so identical source trees produce byte-identical root-drop and onefile manifests regardless of caller order.
evidenceOrRepro: node --strip-types scripts/validate-runner-reproducibility.ts reproduced the failure serially: release/atm-root-drop/release-manifest.json was not byte-identical across consecutive builds. The initial overlapping invocation caused a separate Windows file-write error and was discarded; the serial run reached the deterministic manifest comparison and failed there.
containment: The repair is limited to the root-drop builder and its release artifacts. It does not weaken the reproducibility assertion, exclude generated files from the manifest, or depend on a caller-specific build order.
followUp: Run the runner reproducibility validator after the repair, then rebuild and publish the sealed runner through the runner-sync steward queue before marking frozen publication complete.
